highlights.title: Tim Cook’s Apple: his 10 biggest wins and misses
highlights.description:
Expectations for Tim Cook were almost impossibly high when he stepped in to replace Apple's visionary cofounder in 2011. He inherited a company on a blockbuster run, after Steve Jobs returned and revitalized the Mac, launched the iPod, and oversaw the launch of the iPhone.
Now, after 15 years in the CEO role, Tim Cook is stepping down. He's replaced today by hardware leader John Ternus. Over the course of Cook's tenure, Apple accomplished a lot, with the launch of plenty of new products, features, and services that the company just wouldn't be the same without. There were plenty of ups and downs, but Cook helped cement the company as one of …

highlights.title: John Ternus is now the CEO of Apple
highlights.description:
Apple SVP John Ternus takes over as CEO from Tim Cook. | AFP via Getty Images	

For the first time since 2011, one of the world's most valuable companies has a new leader, as today marks John Ternus' first day as Apple's CEO. He's replacing Tim Cook, who will continue on as the executive chairman on Apple's board and departed with a letter to employees that remarked, "This place is proof that culture triumphs over everything. We share a belief that what we build matters, and that we have both the opportunity and the responsibility to leave the world better than we found it."

business.title: Apple's Vision Pro Layoffs Were Broader Than First Reported
business.description:
Recent layoffs of Apple employees working on the Vision Pro were broader than previously thought, Bloomberg's Mark Gurman reports. 


Last month, Gurman said that Apple cut around 100 jobs from the Vision Products Group, with those cuts centered on the headset's gaming and immersive video teams. Gurman now says the layoffs also reached Vision Pro staff across the rest of the company, including people working on device security, audio engineering, Siri integration, testing, and visionOS. The cuts follow the June departure of Paul Meade, the executive who ran Apple's Vision Pro and smart glasses division, who left Apple for OpenAI.

Gurman reports that people inside the Vision Pro group have spent months lobbying new CEO John Ternus to stay the course on the platform even as sales continue to underwhelm. Colleagues who have discussed the headset with Ternus say he was skeptical of it from the start, seeing it as too bulky and too costly to reach a mass audience.
